responsibility: Defines the Xtensa target’s core machine macros and ABI description used by the GCC middle end and generated backend code. It maps dynamically supplied Xtensa configuration values into TARGET_* feature predicates, declares preprocessor builtins, and specifies the target’s data layout, endianness, register names, alignment rules, calling and exception-handling conventions, assembler output forms, constant-pool behavior, and other compile-time properties that characterize the architecture independently of individual instruction patterns.
same_name_distinction: Among the xtensa.* files, this is the target-definition header that exposes architecture/ABI macros, builtins, data layout, register naming, and assembler conventions to GCC; unlike xtensa.cc it does not implement hooks, unlike xtensa.md it does not encode RTL instruction patterns, and unlike xtensa.opt it does not declare user options.
